citation: Illinois State Archives, Illinois Public Domain Land Tract Sales Database (Springfield: Office of the Secretary of State).
date: database of the federal land office registers
note: The Archives' index to the sales registers of the federal land offices. Each row carries the purchaser as the register wrote it, the purchaser's stated residence (a COUNTY, and most often UNKNOWN), the aliquot part or town lot, section, township, range, meridian, county, acres, price per acre, total price, type of sale, date of purchase, and the register volume and page. This project read it for seven townships of the third principal meridian through 31 December 1836: T39N R14E and T40N R14E, the two the town stands on (T-0557), and the five that ring them — T39N R13E, T38N R14E, T38N R15E, T40N R13E and T41N R14E (T-0677). Two hundred and fifty-two section queries in all. The database's own search returns at most 150 rows per query and offers no paging, which is why the reading is by section and why four sections — T39N R14E 16, 21 and 29, and T39N R13E 16 — are declared unread. T-0677 went back over the search form and confirmed that section is the finest grain it offers: the page's own three searches are section/township/range/meridian, township/range/meridian and county, the county option "cannot be used in combination with any other search criteria", and the result page carries no paging, offset or sort parameter. Reading past the ceiling therefore needs a different source, not a narrower query (T-0678). See data/research/land_sales/README.md. The site refuses this runner's datacentre address outright (403 from every user agent), so the pages were fetched through the public r.jina.ai reader, which returns the origin's own HTML — the access route is recorded on every record's locator and changes nothing about what the page says.
